justification: Standard: new CI infrastructure (a Postgres service container, a migration-apply step, a new blocking job) that changes what every future PR touching this area is checked against. Not Critical: strictly additive, isolated, cannot touch production (no production credential is reachable from this job at all). Not Minor: it closes a named, real coverage gap (write-path has no blocking CI check), not a documentation or wording change.

pre_impl.existing_data: migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql -- the only schema this job touches, applied fresh to an empty Postgres container. Verified locally first (real throwaway local Postgres, not assumed from reading the file): applies cleanly to a bare database with no prior tables or extensions -- gen_random_uuid() is native since Postgres 13, no pgcrypto or other extension needed.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The isolated test database's schema is exactly migration 033, nothing more -- if services/drawdown_verify.py ever assumes a column or table this migration does not create, this job would fail loudly (a real, useful signal) rather than silently pass against a schema that happens to differ from what production actually has.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: N/A -- CI-only change, no application code, no data model change.
pre_impl.external_source_error: N/A -- no external service, the Postgres container is local to the job and torn down when it ends.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: N/A -- CI infrastructure, not a user-facing code path.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Run against a throwaway local Postgres database created for exactly this purpose (drawdown_ci_test), BEFORE the migration was applied -- the write-path tests need the table to exist, mirroring what would happen in CI if the migration-apply step were broken or skipped.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before applying migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql to drawdown_ci_test: both tests fail with psycopg2.errors.UndefinedTable (relation "drawdown_verify_audits" does not exist), the same real error class DQ-91's original bug was about, now reproduced against an isolated database rather than production. After running the migration-apply step's exact python one-liner against the same database: both tests pass. Database dropped afterward (DROP DATABASE drawdown_ci_test), confirming this test methodology itself leaves nothing behind either.

functions.name: Apply migration 033 to the isolated test database (inline step, .github/workflows/gates.yml)
functions.input: migrations/033_drawdown_verify_audits.sql read from disk, executed against the job's own Postgres service container
functions.output: Asserts the table now exists (count=1 from information_schema.tables) before printing success and before any test runs -- a broken apply fails loudly at this explicit check, not confusingly inside a later test
functions.if_none: N/A -- the migration file path is a hardcoded literal checked into the repo, not optional input

queries.purpose: Apply migration 033 to the isolated container and confirm the table was actually created before running any test against it
queries.file_line: .github/workflows/gates.yml, 'Apply migration 033 to the isolated test database' step
queries.if_zero: The step's own assert fails loudly (migration did not create the table) before any test runs against a database that silently lacks the schema it needs
queries.if_wrong: N/A -- boolean existence check, not a value that can be 'wrong' short of being absent

break_it.scenario: The isolated test database's schema (migration 033 only) drifts from production's real live schema -- someone alters the production table directly (not via a new migration file) or a future migration changes it without this file being updated.
break_it.what_happens: This job would keep passing against a schema that no longer matches what services/drawdown_verify.py actually runs against in production, giving false confidence.
break_it.how: NOT structurally mitigated -- there is no automatic check that migration 033 still matches production's live schema. Mitigated TODAY only: production was verified column-for-column against migration 033 when the migration was run this session (PR #1038). A drift-detection check (comparing the isolated schema against a live production schema snapshot) would close this properly and was not built here -- named, not silently assumed away.
break_it.repro: N/A -- a schema-drift scenario, not something the current tooling reproduces

break_it.scenario: The Postgres service container fails to become healthy in time, or the migration-apply step silently does nothing (e.g. wrong DATABASE_URL, empty file).
break_it.what_happens: Tests would fail with a connection or UndefinedTable error either way -- not a silent pass, but the failure message might not clearly say WHY.
break_it.how: The migration-apply step asserts the table actually exists (count=1) before printing success and before any test runs, so a broken apply step fails at that explicit assertion with a clear message, not three steps later inside a test with a more confusing traceback
break_it.repro: N/A -- verified locally that the migration applies and creates exactly this table; the assert exists specifically to make a future breakage loud rather than confusing

break_it.scenario: This job accidentally points at production instead of the isolated container (e.g. DATABASE_URL typo, wrong secret reference).
break_it.what_happens: Could write test rows to production, or worse, could not (if it did, it would be the exact DQ-91-class risk this whole session has been closing).
break_it.how: DATABASE_URL in this job is assembled at runtime from job-level env vars (PGHOST_TEST/PGPORT_TEST/PGUSER_TEST/PGPASSWORD_TEST/PGDATABASE_TEST, all pointing at the job's own localhost service container) -- it never references secrets.DATABASE_URL anywhere in this job, so there is no production secret to typo or misreference in the first place
break_it.repro: grep -A20 "drawdown-verify-write-path:" .github/workflows/gates.yml -- no secrets. reference anywhere in this job

break_it.scenario: The first real CI run of this job (PR #1040, run 33840764610) failed in 12s: 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at unix:///var/run/docker.sock' -- the shared ${{ vars.RUNNER_LABEL || 'ubuntu-latest' }} pattern every other job in this file uses resolved to a self-hosted runner (wsl-ubuntu-lawre-2, named in the failure log) with no Docker daemon running, so the `services:` Postgres container -- which GitHub Actions implements via Docker -- could never start.
break_it.what_happens: The job fails every single run, forever, on this repo's actual CI infrastructure -- not a flaky failure, a structural one. Local validation (a real throwaway Postgres, twice) could not catch this because it never involved the self-hosted-runner/Docker question at all.
break_it.how: runs-on hardcoded to `ubuntu-latest` (GitHub-hosted) for this one job only, not the shared RUNNER_LABEL pattern -- GitHub-hosted runners ship Docker pre-installed and running by default, which is the whole mechanism `services:` depends on. Every other job in this file keeps using the fast self-hosted runner; only this one needs hosted infrastructure specifically for Docker.
break_it.repro: gh run view 33840764610 --log -- the exact failure, timestamped, before this fix; re-run after push confirms whether ubuntu-latest resolves the Docker dependency

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- the YAML's `services:` container syntax was validated for parse-correctness locally (python yaml.safe_load) and the exact SQL/test logic was proven against a real local Postgres database first, but the full GitHub Actions service-container startup and networking (health check, port mapping, job-to-service connectivity) can only be confirmed by an actual CI run, which happens automatically once this PR is opened -- checked immediately after push, before merge, not assumed.
